Every time I try to think about what I want to do after graduation, my mind just goes completely foggy and shuts down. I have no ambition, no dream company, no target package—just this heavy, suffocating emptiness.
sandhi_response: When your mind fogs up and shuts down, it is often trying to protect you from the overwhelming pressure of needing immediate answers. Let's step back from the massive 'after graduation' questions and just focus on breathing through this single moment.

user_input: My mom spent an hour on the phone yesterday talking about how my cousin just landed a 12 LPA package at some fintech startup, and then she asked me what my 'plan' is. I lied and said I was preparing for GATE, but the truth is I don't want to do GATE, I don't want to do coding, and I don't know what the hell I'm doing with my life. I feel like a fraud who is just wasting my parents' hard-earned money because I don't have a single goal to work toward. I'm just waking up, scrolling, attending mandatory attendance lectures, and going back to sleep.
sandhi_response: It hurts so deeply to carry the weight of expectations when you are still trying to find your own footing. You are not a fraud for needing time to discover your path, even if the silence right now feels loud and unsettling.

user_input: I have two backlogs from last semester and the remedial exams are next month, but I just can't bring myself to open the books. It's not even that the syllabus is too hard, it's just that I don't see the point anymore. I feel completely hollow, like a passenger in my own body just watching the semesters pass by while I sink deeper into this hole.
sandhi_response: Feeling like a passenger in your own body is a sign of deep exhaustion, where even small tasks feel like climbing a mountain. Let's lay down the burden of 'finding a passion' for now and simply focus on finding a little bit of comfort in this present physical space.

user_input: Our class WhatsApp group is just a constant stream of 'congratulations' messages for people clearing the first round of campus placements or getting tech society leads. Every time I see those notifications, my chest gets so tight. I haven't even made a resume yet because I don't know what to put on it—I don't have any achievements, projects, or even a vague direction of where I want to go. I feel like I'm standing still on a fast-moving escalator and everyone is just rushing past me while I freeze.
sandhi_response: Watching everyone else rush forward can make your own stillness feel like a failure, but your journey doesn't have to match their speed. It is safe to mute the noise for a moment and allow yourself to breathe at your own natural pace.

user_input: Honestly, what am I even doing? Everyone in my wing is grindin Leetcode, talking about 20 LPA packages, and I can't even force myself to open a compiler. user_input: Midterms start next week and I haven't touched a single slide of DBMS or OS. It’s not even like I’m lazy, it’s just... why? What is the goal here? user_input: My roommate just got an internship at a FAANG company and my whole WhatsApp group is exploding with congratulatory messages. sandhi_response: It hurts deeply when everyone else's milestones only seem to magnify your own feelings of being lost and stuck. It is completely natural to withdraw when you don't know where you are heading, but your worth is not tied to having a dream company or a flawless coding run.

user_input: I have three backlogs from last semester and the remedial exams are in two weeks. user_input: Our lab instructor just put up the grading curve for the compiler design project, and I’m right at the bottom. Honestly, I didn't even cry. I just feel this weird, empty numbness.
